  "text": "When Helen arrived, her sister was taking the curtains down.

“I thought we were doing the cupboards,” Helen said.

“We are.”

Ruth stood on their mother's footstool, one arm raised. Three hooks lay on the windowsill.

“Hold this.”

Helen took the curtain's weight. The lining was yellow except where the folds had kept it hidden.

“Someone might want them,” Ruth said.

“They're too short for my windows.”

“I didn't mean you.”

They spread the curtains across the sofa. Without them, the room looked wider and the glass looked dirty.

In the kitchen, Helen opened a cupboard. There were six jars of marmalade, each labelled in their mother's handwriting.

“Did you know she was still making it?”

Ruth climbed down from the stool.

“I bought the oranges.”

Helen turned a jar until the label faced away.

Outside, a van slowed beside the house, then continued along the street.

“They said between nine and eleven,” Ruth said.

“It's only quarter past.”

“I know.”

Helen found newspaper beneath the sink and began wrapping the jars.

“You don't need to wrap those. They're going in my car.”

“They'll knock together.”

Ruth watched her fold the paper over a lid.

“Leave one out.”

Helen set a jar beside the kettle.

“Have you had breakfast?”

“Not yet.”

The bread bin was empty. Helen checked the freezer and found two slices in a bag, with a heel between them.

“Toast?”

Ruth nodded and went to the drawer for knives.

Helen put the slices in the toaster. Her sister stayed beside the open drawer, holding the knife with the loose handle.

“She never did get this fixed.”"
